notes: THE FIRST GENUINELY INDEPENDENT REVIEW IN THIS REPOSITORY. Thirteen records precede it; every one was written by a subagent of its own author, and nine did not say so. This reviewer was dispatched by a DIFFERENT SESSION (a peer session's orchestrator, token 3b64530b), working read-only in its own scratch clone. CORRECTION, MADE AT THE REVIEWER'S INSISTENCE: an earlier version of this record claimed 'its text is reproduced as it wrote it' while in fact paraphrasing, said it found false claims in FOUR places when it reported THREE, and attributed a quotation to the PR description that the PR never contained. The reviewer caught all three misstatements in the record that exists to preserve its words. Its findings are therefore quoted below rather than summarised. VERDICT, verbatim: 'As a report-only gate it is sound. When nothing is checked it says so, both in words and with its own exit code (2, separate from 0). I found no case where it reports success after checking nothing. There are four defects, none of which blocks a report-only merge. Three have to be fixed before this gate is made blocking. Finding 5 is a set of false claims in the PR description.' FINDING 1, verbatim: 'One real pass hides uncomparable commands (PLAUSIBLE risk; the behaviour is reproduced). In scripts/lwb_check_proof.py, UNCOMPARABLE commands count toward neither failures nor the re-executed total. So one real pass next to a drifted command still prints the success summary ... If the sanitiser version changes, every old digest becomes uncomparable while exit stays 0. Before this gate blocks, uncomparable commands should get their own count in the TOTAL line or their own exit code.' FINDING 2, verbatim: 'Empty output and expected errors pass (by design; not a defect as report-only). ... The gate proves the output reproduces, not that the command checks anything.' FINDING 3, verbatim: 'The recursion guard can be bypassed (CONFIRMED). _command_resolves_to_self compares only the exact file name of each argv token (Path(a).name == "lwb_check_proof.py"), case-sensitively.' It listed ['python','scripts/LWB_CHECK_PROOF.PY'] -- 'This one was actually re-executed rather than skipped' -- plus ['python','-m','lwb_check_proof'], a bash -c wrapper and a subprocess.run wrapper, adding: 'Such a record would re-run --reexecute over itself with no depth limit, so it would never end. I did not execute the unbounded case. Add to this that subprocess.run has no timeout ... so a hanging command stalls the CI job even with continue-on-error.' FINDING 4, verbatim: 'A record with no argv crashes the run (CONFIRMED). ... The whole run dies with a traceback (exit 1), so this can never be misread as a pass.' FINDING 5, THREE false statements in the PR description, verbatim: 'It says TOTAL: 3 of 101 commands re-executed across 12 records and FAIL: proof/20.json ... digest mismatch. The actual result at the head is 4 of 107 ... 13 records ... ALL RE-EXECUTED COMMANDS MATCHED, exit 0, and proof/20.json shows 2 PASS. It says "Only proof/20.json carries the flag". proof/21.json also has 2 verifiable commands. It says "351 tests pass". Commit dc43983 says "364 tests pass". The commit messages match what I measured. The "mismatch it found" is real history, but the description presents it as the current state.' THREE SUBAGENT REVIEW PASSES HAD READ THAT DESCRIPTION AND CAUGHT NONE OF IT. Correcting it is what sent the author to look at CI, which is how an eleven-commit CI blackout was found. RE-CHECK AT 0b1aadf, verbatim: 'AGREE still stands at 0b1aadf, for the report-only gate code, which is unchanged. But 0b1aadf is not "only the quoting change": there is a second commit in between, and it edits the review record that quotes me.' The author had described the delta as one line; it was two commits. The reviewer confirmed the ci.yml change is exactly one line, that ci.yml at ab0f875 does not parse ('mapping values are not allowed here') and all three workflow files parse at 0b1aadf, so 'the fix is real'. FIRST OBSERVED LINUX REPRODUCTION OF THE DIGESTS, verbatim: 'Re-execution on the ubuntu 3.12 runner: the step succeeded with TOTAL: 4 of 107 commands re-executed across 13 records -- ALL RE-EXECUTED COMMANDS MATCHED. That is the first observed Linux reproduction of the digests. I did not check the macOS or Windows logs.' This is the evidence the blocking PR requires and that no reviewer could previously supply. NOT CHECKED, verbatim: 'Linux or runner reproduction of the digests, and the CI run itself. The test suite (I did not run pytest). The pr-authority rename/modify logic (_proof_path_statuses). Whether each of the "four ways" tests fails without its guard. Arbitrary argv in a PR's proof record running in CI.' The first item was subsequently satisfied by the re-check above. DISPOSITION: findings 1, 3 and 4 are recorded in the PR body as defects that MUST be fixed before this gate is ever made blocking. They are deliberately not fixed in this PR: it is report-only, none can cause a false pass in that mode, and this repo has twice lost a PR to unbounded scope. The reviewer's judgement that they do not block a report-only merge is recorded as the reviewer's, not the author's.
